preconditions.necessity: The overflow is triggered by stdin input to gets(). Without stdin access, the vulnerability cannot be triggered.

preconditions.description: Attacker provides at least 76 bytes of input (0x4c bytes from buffer start to saved ra at sp+0x64)
preconditions.necessity: 76 bytes is the minimum to reach saved ra. Fewer bytes only corrupt the buffer and padding without reaching saved registers.

preconditions.description: main function has no stack canary (does not reference __stack_chk_guard at 0x490958)
preconditions.necessity: Without canary, the overflow is not detected at runtime. main's prologue/epilogue contain no canary check, confirmed by disassembly.

preconditions.description: gets() performs unbounded read (no size parameter, reads until newline/EOF)
preconditions.necessity: gets is inherently unbounded — it has no size parameter and reads until newline or EOF, allowing arbitrary-length overflow.

alias_key_findings.alias: The 76-byte gap is the critical offset. Input bytes [0:72] are buffer+padding, bytes [72:76] overwrite saved fp, bytes [76:80] overwrite saved ra, bytes [80:] control stack beyond ra.
alias_key_findings.implication: Attacker controls saved fp, saved ra, and ROP chain space with a single gets() call. The 76-byte offset is the key precondition for all stack control primitives.

alias_key_findings.expression: saved_gp at sp+0x10 is BEFORE buffer at sp+0x18
alias_key_findings.alias: saved gp is at sp+0x10, which is 8 bytes before the buffer start at sp+0x18. Forward overflow from the buffer does NOT overwrite saved gp.
alias_key_findings.implication: gp remains intact after overflow. Gadgets using gp-relative addressing will have a valid gp value. This is beneficial for ROP chain construction (S4 concern).

verification_plan.method: Unicorn Engine MIPS32 BE CPU emulation. Load binary code/data segments, set up stack, hook gets() to inject attacker input, execute main() from 0x4007a0 through epilogue (jr $ra at 0x40084c). Observe saved ra at sp+0x64, saved fp at sp+0x60, and stack content beyond ra via memory reads. Verify ra register value at jr $ra instruction.
verification_plan.environment: Python3 + Unicorn Engine (MIPS32 big-endian mode). Binary cannot run natively (MIPS BE on x86 host, no qemu-mips available). Unicorn executes actual binary code from .text segment.
expected_evidence: PRIM-001: short input (20 bytes) leaves saved_ra = 0xdeadbeef (original, not overwritten) — proves overflow is required
PRIM-001: stack[sp+0x68]=0x0041f340, stack[sp+0x6c]=0x00477504, stack[sp+0x70]=0x00000fab — extended stack control verified

mitigations.name: Stack Canary (__stack_chk_guard)
mitigations.primitive_impact: main does NOT reference __stack_chk_guard (0x490958). No canary check in main's prologue/epilogue. The stack overflow is completely undetected at runtime. STACK_CONTROL primitive is fully viable.

mitigations.name: NX (No-Execute Stack)
mitigations.primitive_impact: NX is disabled (no GNU_STACK segment, RWX segments present, first LOAD segment is R E). Stack is executable. This means shellcode-on-stack is also viable, but does not affect STACK_CONTROL or RIP_CONTROL primitives which work regardless of NX.

mitigations.name: PIE (Position Independent Executable)
mitigations.primitive_impact: No PIE — EXEC type with fixed base 0x400000. All code, data, and gadget addresses are at fixed, known locations. This makes ROP chain construction straightforward (no ASLR to defeat for code/data addresses).

mitigations.name: RELRO
mitigations.primitive_impact: Only Partial RELRO. The .got section at 0x4922c0 is writable. This allows GOT overwrite as an alternative control-flow hijack method, but is not needed for the current STACK_CONTROL/RIP_CONTROL primitives.

mitigations.name: FORTIFY
mitigations.primitive_impact: No FORTIFY_SOURCE. gets() is not replaced with a fortified version. The unbounded read proceeds without any runtime size check.

evidence.description: main prologue: addiu $sp,$sp,-0x68; sw $ra,0x64($sp); sw $fp,0x60($sp); move $fp,$sp. Stack frame size 0x68=104 bytes. Saved ra at sp+0x64, saved fp at sp+0x60, buffer at fp+0x18=sp+0x18. Buffer-to-ra distance = 0x64-0x18 = 0x4c = 76 bytes.
gets call site: addiu $v0,$fp,0x18; move $a0,$v0; lw $v0,-0x7f94($gp); move $t9,$v0; bal 0x408ce0. Buffer argument is fp+0x18=sp+0x18. gets (_IO_gets @ 0x408ce0) is called with no size parameter.
main epilogue: lw $ra,0x64($sp); lw $fp,0x60($sp); addiu $sp,$sp,0x68; jr $ra. The saved ra is loaded from sp+0x64 (which was overwritten by overflow) and used as the jr $ra jump target.

main does NOT reference __stack_chk_guard (0x490958). No canary load/store/compare in main's prologue or epilogue. Confirmed by full disassembly of main (0x4007a0-0x400850): no lui/lw/sw involving 0x490958 or gp-relative offset -0x9958.

Unicorn emulation: With 80-byte input (76 padding + 0x41414141), saved_ra @ sp+0x64 = 0x41414141 (attacker-controlled). ra register at jr $ra (0x40084c) = 0x41414141. With 20-byte input, saved_ra = 0xdeadbeef (original, not overwritten). Proves overflow of 76+ bytes is required and sufficient to control saved ra.

Unicorn emulation: With 80-byte input (72 padding + 0x45454545 for fp + 0x41414141 for ra), saved_fp @ sp+0x60 = 0x45454545 and saved_ra @ sp+0x64 = 0x41414141. Both saved registers are attacker-controlled.

Unicorn emulation: With 92-byte input (76 padding + 0x004010c4 ra + 0x0041f340 + 0x00477504 + 0x00000fab), stack[sp+0x68]=0x0041f340, stack[sp+0x6c]=0x00477504, stack[sp+0x70]=0x00000fab. Extended stack content beyond ra is fully attacker-controlled, enabling ROP chain construction.

verification_result.details: Unicorn MIPS32 BE emulation of main() with overflow input. Test 1 (20 bytes): saved_ra=0xdeadbeef (not overwritten). Test 3 (80 bytes): saved_ra=0x41414141, ra_at_jr=0x41414141. fp test: saved_fp=0x45454545. Extended stack: sp+0x68=0x0041f340, sp+0x6c=0x00477504, sp+0x70=0x00000fab. All values match attacker-specified inputs. STACK_CONTROL VERIFIED: attacker controls saved fp, saved ra, and arbitrary stack content beyond ra.

primitives.notes: STACK_CONTROL is a DIRECT primitive: the gets() overflow directly writes attacker-controlled bytes to saved fp (sp+0x60), saved ra (sp+0x64), and stack beyond ra (sp+0x68+). No intermediate object reuse or metadata manipulation is involved. The 76-byte offset from buffer to saved ra is the critical precondition. PRIM-001 merges three sub-tests (ra overwrite, fp overwrite, extended stack control) as they share the same BUG, root cause, preconditions, and target operation. The off-by-one null byte effect (Test 2: 76 bytes causes gets null-terminator to partially overwrite ra's MSB) is a minor side effect of gets() null-termination, not a separate primitive.

source.root_cause: STACK_BUFFER_OVERFLOW: gets() overflow overwrites saved ra at sp+0x64. main's epilogue loads the overwritten ra via lw $ra,0x64($sp) and jumps to it via jr $ra. Since the overwritten ra value is fully attacker-controlled, the jump target is attacker-controlled.
source.description: The stack buffer overflow via gets() overwrites the saved return address (ra) at sp+0x64 with an attacker-specified value. When main returns, its epilogue executes lw $ra,0x64($sp); jr $ra, loading the attacker-controlled value into $ra and jumping to that address. This is direct control-flow hijack via return address overwrite.

chain: BUG-001: gets() unbounded stack buffer write at 0x40082c
Root Cause: gets reads stdin into sp+0x18 with no length limit; saved ra at sp+0x64 is 76 bytes away
Memory Primitive: attacker-controlled write to saved ra at sp+0x64
Controlled Operation: main epilogue at 0x400840 executes lw $ra,0x64($sp) loading attacker value, then jr $ra at 0x40084c jumps to attacker-controlled address
Primitive: RIP_CONTROL — $ra register == attacker-specified value at jr $ra instruction

controlled_element.what: return address ($ra register at jr $ra instruction in main's epilogue)
controlled_element.how: Attacker provides 76+ bytes via stdin to gets(). Bytes 76-79 of the input overwrite saved ra at sp+0x64. main's epilogue loads this value into $ra and jumps to it via jr $ra.

preconditions.description: Attacker can provide input via stdin to the program (gets reads from stdin)
preconditions.necessity: The overflow is triggered by stdin input to gets(). Without stdin access, the vulnerability cannot be triggered.

preconditions.description: Attacker provides at least 80 bytes of input (76 bytes padding + 4 bytes for ra)
preconditions.necessity: 76 bytes reaches saved ra; 4 additional bytes provide the new ra value. Total 80 bytes minimum for full ra control.

preconditions.description: main function has no stack canary (does not reference __stack_chk_guard)
preconditions.necessity: Without canary, the overflow of saved ra is not detected. main's prologue/epilogue contain no canary check.

preconditions.description: main's epilogue executes lw $ra,0x64($sp); jr $ra — loading and using the overwritten ra
preconditions.necessity: The overwritten ra must be loaded and used for a jump. main's epilogue at 0x400840-0x40084c does exactly this.

preconditions.description: No PIE — target addresses are at fixed, known locations (base 0x400000)
preconditions.necessity: For RIP_CONTROL to be useful for exploitation, the attacker must know valid target addresses. No PIE means all code/gadget addresses are fixed and known.

alias_key_findings.expression: jr $ra at 0x40084c uses $ra loaded from sp+0x64 (overwritten by overflow)
alias_key_findings.alias: The jr $ra instruction in main's epilogue is the control-flow hijack point. $ra is loaded from sp+0x64 which is directly overwritten by the gets() overflow at offset 76.
alias_key_findings.implication: The hijack is immediate and direct: overflow → saved ra overwrite → epilogue loads ra → jr $ra jumps to attacker address. No intermediate dereference or indirection.

verification_plan.method: Unicorn Engine MIPS32 BE CPU emulation. Execute main() with overflow input containing two different target addresses (Y1=0x41414141, Y2=0x42424242). Verify that $ra register at jr $ra instruction (0x40084c) equals the attacker-specified address in both cases.
verification_plan.environment: Python3 + Unicorn Engine (MIPS32 big-endian mode). Binary cannot run natively (MIPS BE on x86 host).
expected_evidence: Two different addresses both successfully loaded into $ra, proving address is controllable

mitigations.name: Stack Canary (__stack_chk_guard)
mitigations.primitive_impact: main has no canary. The ra overwrite is not detected. RIP_CONTROL via ra overwrite is fully viable.

mitigations.name: NX (No-Execute Stack)
mitigations.primitive_impact: NX disabled. Both ROP (jumping to code at fixed addresses) and shellcode-on-stack are viable hijack targets. RIP_CONTROL itself is unaffected by NX — it controls where jr $ra jumps, regardless of whether the target is code or data.

mitigations.name: PIE (Position Independent Executable)
mitigations.primitive_impact: No PIE. All gadget addresses (e.g., ret2csu epilogue at 0x4010c4, syscall gadget at 0x41f340) are at fixed, known locations. The attacker can specify exact jump targets without needing to defeat ASLR.

mitigations.name: ASLR
mitigations.primitive_impact: Stack ASLR may be enabled on the target kernel, randomizing the stack base address. However, this does NOT affect RIP_CONTROL via ROP: all code/gadget addresses are fixed (no PIE), and the overflow writes to the current stack frame relative to $sp, so the ra overwrite works regardless of stack base. Stack ASLR only affects shellcode-on-stack (which needs to know the exact stack address), not ROP.

evidence.description: main epilogue: lw $ra,0x64($sp); lw $fp,0x60($sp); addiu $sp,$sp,0x68; jr $ra. The saved ra is loaded from sp+0x64 (overwritten by overflow) and used as jr $ra target. This is the control-flow hijack instruction.
Unicorn emulation Test 1: Input = 76 bytes padding + 0x41414141. At jr $ra (0x40084c), $ra register = 0x41414141 (== attacker-specified Y1). PASS.

Unicorn emulation Test 2: Input = 76 bytes padding + 0x42424242. At jr $ra (0x40084c), $ra register = 0x42424242 (== attacker-specified Y2). PASS. Two different addresses both successfully loaded into $ra, proving the jump target is fully attacker-controlled.

verification_result.written_value: 0x41414141 (Y1) and 0x42424242 (Y2) written to saved ra at sp+0x64
verification_result.details: Unicorn MIPS32 BE emulation of main() with two different overflow payloads. Test 1: Y1=0x41414141 -> $ra at jr $ra = 0x41414141. Test 2: Y2=0x42424242 -> $ra at jr $ra = 0x42424242. Both tests PASS. RIP_CONTROL VERIFIED: attacker controls the jump target of jr $ra by overwriting saved ra at sp+0x64 via gets() overflow.

primitives.notes: RIP_CONTROL is a DIRECT primitive: the gets() overflow directly overwrites saved ra, and main's epilogue directly loads and jumps to it via jr $ra. No intermediate steps (no tcache, no object reuse, no metadata manipulation). The verification uses two different target addresses (Y1=0x41414141, Y2=0x42424242) to prove the address is controllable, satisfying the RIP_CONTROL acceptance standard (register value == attacker-specified value). Note: This is MIPS 32-bit, so this is technically EIP_CONTROL equivalent (32-bit instruction pointer), but using RIP_CONTROL as the generic primitive type per the schema. The actual register is $ra (return address register) which serves the same function as EIP/RIP on x86.

non_primitives.reason: While NX is disabled and the stack is executable (making shellcode-on-stack theoretically viable), CODE_EXECUTION via shellcode requires knowing the exact stack address for the jump. Stack ASLR (if enabled on target) would randomize this. ROP (via RIP_CONTROL + STACK_CONTROL) is the more reliable primitive and does not require knowing the stack address. Shellcode execution is an S4 exploit route concern, not a separate S3 primitive. The underlying primitives (STACK_CONTROL + RIP_CONTROL) are already verified.

Partial RELRO means .got is writable at 0x4922c0. However, the gets() overflow writes to the stack, not to .got. To overwrite GOT entries, the attacker would need an arbitrary write primitive targeting .got addresses, which is not directly provided by the stack overflow. GOT overwrite would require chaining STACK_CONTROL + RIP_CONTROL into a ROP chain that performs the write (S4 concern). The direct primitive from BUG-001 is stack control + control-flow hijack, not GOT overwrite.

unresolved.description: Target runtime stack ASLR status not confirmed
unresolved.reason: The binary is MIPS BE and cannot run natively in the current x86 environment (no qemu-mips available). Stack ASLR status on the target kernel is unknown. However, this does not affect the verified primitives: STACK_CONTROL and RIP_CONTROL work relative to $sp and use fixed code addresses (no PIE), so they are valid regardless of stack ASLR.
unresolved.required_next_step: S4 should confirm stack ASLR status if shellcode-on-stack is attempted. For ROP-based exploitation (using fixed gadget addresses), stack ASLR is irrelevant.

unresolved.description: MIPS cache coherency for self-modifying code
unresolved.reason: MIPS architecture requires explicit I-cache flush for self-modifying code (shellcode on stack). If S4 attempts shellcode execution, the I-cache may contain stale instructions. This is a MIPS-specific concern for shellcode, not for ROP.
unresolved.required_next_step: S4 should use ROP (no cache coherency issue) or include cache flush gadgets if shellcode is attempted.
